svg.title: From a commit to Cape Town
svg.desc: From a commit to Cape Town, in three lanes: Laptop, GitHub (KatlehoKomeke/Appointment-Booking-System) and AWS. Everything is built except one dashed region marked planned after M6. Step A, along the top: the administrator, branchbook-admin signed in with aws login, runs cdk deploy BranchbookAccount by hand with BRANCHBOOK_ALERT_EMAIL set. Laptop: step 1, git commit. Step 2, the pre-commit hook refuses .env files, keys, .claude/ and cdk.context.json, then runs gitleaks on the staged diff; it fails closed, and a refused edge leads to 'commit refused: a finding, or no scanner'. Step 3, the post-commit hook prints a reminder after a major commit and never blocks. A caveat note joined to both hooks: they are opt-in (make hooks), and --no-verify skips the pre-commit hook. Step 4, git push, the start of the main path, which crosses into GitHub. GitHub: a small file, aws-connection-check.yml, runs only by hand. Step 5, push protection refuses known provider secrets; a refused edge leads to 'push rejected'. Step 6, main, with a warning: force-push refused, no required checks; every push starts the workflows below together. ci.yml with jobs api, web and stack runs application checks with no AWS access. secret-scan.yml with job gitleaks scans the full history after the push and blocks nothing. infra.yml with job test-and-synth runs only if infra/** or infra.yml changed. deploy.yml carries the gap: it does not wait for ci. Step 7, its test job runs CDK lint, tsc and Jest; deploy needs test. Step 8, the deploy job passes the gate environment aws-demo, which allows main and v* tags only. Dependabot opens weekly pull requests; ci and secret-scan run on them, and deploy never does. AWS: the main path carries an OIDC token from token.actions.githubusercontent.com to step 9, AWS STS, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, which returns credentials for at most 1 h; a dotted line joins STS to the role's trust policy. In AWS · us-east-1 (N. Virginia), the BranchbookAccount stack holds the IAM OIDC provider GitHubOidcProvider, the AWS Budgets budget branchbook-monthly and the IAM role branchbook-github-deploy, whose trust policy requires aud and sub to match; IAM is global, and its stack lives in us-east-1. In AWS · af-south-1 (Cape Town): step 10, the CDK bootstrap roles (file-publishing and deploy) hand over to AWS CloudFormation, which acts as the cfn-exec role. Step 11, the BranchbookRelease stack holds /branchbook/release = GITHUB_SHA, the highlighted node. Step 12, the main path returns to the deploy job: verify that the value equals GITHUB_SHA, else the job fails. Below it, dashed and planned after M6: BranchbookDns, BranchbookData and BranchbookApp join this job. ci, secret-scan and deploy passed on the push of 85cd726, 25 October 2026.
